key_insight: A lightweight, multimodal-aware conversion lets existing vision–language models replace bulky multi-head Key-Value caches with compact Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), achieving large memory and latency savings without costly pretraining.
problem_solved: Addresses the exploding KV-cache memory and inference-time compute in VLMs when handling long or multimodal contexts, enabling practical deployment and faster inference.
method: Introduce a parameter-efficient MHA→MLA adaptation that maps existing Multi-Head Attention KV structures into a compact latent-attention representation.
Use small multimodal-aware adapter/projection modules and alignment objectives so models can be converted with minimal fine-tuning rather than full pretraining.
Design conversion and inference routines that maintain cross-modal fidelity while drastically reducing KV storage and attention computation.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy VLMs with much lower memory footprint and faster inference (longer contexts, lower latency) using only lightweight fine-tuning—reducing cost and making multimodal applications more scalable.

paper_title: MHA2MLA-VLM: Enabling DeepSeek's Economical Multi-Head Latent Attention across Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Xiaoran Fan, Zhichao Sun, Tao Ji, Lixing Shen, Tao Gui
